name: Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Association v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co.
summary: The Supreme Court held that courts must set aside agency actions that are arbitrary and capricious, meaning the agency failed to consider relevant factors or offered an explanation that runs counter to the evidence.
significance: This case established the 'arbitrary and capricious' standard of judicial review for agency decisions under the Administrative Procedure Act, the standard the Ninth Circuit applied when finding the military's environmental review deficient.
